title: Product Designer, AWS Search, Security, Observability, Governance
note: Dublin product designer role pitched at growing designers (guidance from senior designers, no years stated): own features end to end, prototype, usability test, extend the design system with PM and engineering, matching his HRMS SaaS work. Domain is very technical (CloudWatch observability and an AI DevOps agent), and a basic qualification is prototyping in code (HTML/JS/CSS or Axure), which only his Callback web app covers, so treat it as a mild stretch. Work pattern and right-to-work terms not stated; ask about sponsorship given Stamp 1G is pending.

title: Product Designer (UX Designer)
note: Core fit: entry-level product designer on a new B2B reseller platform (self-service portals, dashboards, contract workflows), with interviews, journey maps, usability testing and Figma prototyping, matching his Partner Portal and HRMS SaaS work. Hybrid Dublin/Letterkenny. Right-to-work flag: posting says you must already be eligible to work in Ireland indefinitely without restrictions, so check before applying while Stamp 1G is pending.

title: Product Designer (new product)
note: Fit: listed as entry level and remote for Ireland, no years stated. End-to-end web and mobile UI/UX, dashboards, a design system and marketing creatives, which matches his Partner Portal dashboards, Mewurk design-system work and Tatos marketing graphics. Caveats: crypto staking and trading-terminal domain, and it's a contractor (consultancy) agreement rather than employment.

title: Junior Product Designer
note: Core fit: explicitly junior/early-career product designer at an Irish-headquartered venture group, covering research, user flows, wireframes, prototypes and high-fidelity UI in Figma (components, auto layout, variants), design systems, interviews and usability testing. B2B SaaS patterns listed as desirable. Remote-first; residency: must be based in Ireland, the UK or Bulgaria (Ireland is fine). They also want hands-on familiarity with AI design tools such as Claude, which isn't on his CV, so show it in the portfolio or cover note. Apply by email to jobs@hibernia-labs.com with CV, portfolio and a short note on a product he admires. No right-to-work requirement stated.

title: Product Designer (junior to senior)
note: Core fit: the posting welcomes junior designers (defined projects with guidance) to make complex education software clear and usable: user flows across user roles, Figma prototypes with components, responsive and accessible UI, working within a design system and reviewing implementation with engineers. Matches his HRMS and Partner Portal work and the education-sector CRM for schools; mission-driven edtech. Fully remote, open to candidates anywhere with regular working-hour overlap with the team (window confirmed early in the process, so check time zones). No right-to-work requirement stated.

title: Product Designer (Product Design Intern, part-time)
note: Lower priority, but a real entry-level product design role in Dublin: part-time internship at a Trinity spinout, open to recent graduates in UX/interaction design. Work is redesigning an analytics dashboard, onboarding and core user flows for non-technical marketers, quick user research and usability tests, and a design system in Figma, which suits his Partner Portal dashboards and HRMS work. Only 3–10 hours a week, so it could sit alongside a main job search. No right-to-work requirement stated.

title: Service Designer (Freelance / Part-time)
note: Small Dublin service design consultancy (government, health, energy) working directly with Gerry Scullion. Explicitly welcomes people who studied service design but haven't worked as one yet, which fits his MSc Design Innovation, The Kept Promise and Spot-to-Plot. Mild stretch: experienced service designers have the edge, and it asks for facilitation, which isn't on his CV. Must live in or near Dublin (he does). Ad-hoc, project-based paid work, not a permanent job. They want no CV: just an email with an intro, an honest self-assessment and a LinkedIn link. No closing date. No right-to-work requirement stated.

title: Interaction Designer (The Dock)
note: Interaction designer at Accenture's R&D hub, The Dock, in Grand Canal Dock. The posting asks for a design qualification or equivalent experience, Figma, Adobe and service design principles, with no minimum years. It matches his MSc service design work and his HRMS end-to-end UX. Stretch: no level is stated (support/contribute wording reads junior-to-mid). Portfolio required. No right-to-work wording.

title: Product Designer (Platform)
note: Internal tools and back-office platform design (support, ops, AI tooling). This maps well onto his in-house HRMS modules and Partner Portal dashboards, and the posting lists a CS degree as nice to have. Stretch: it asks for 3+ years (he has about 2 plus the MSc). Remote position based in Ireland, so you must live in Ireland. No sponsorship wording.

title: Associate Product Manager (Cost Management)
note: Stretch: PM role, and it asks for 1+ year in product management or 2+ years in a customer-facing role, while his experience is in design. Still a reasonable fit for B2B SaaS: partnering with UX designers and engineers, customer discovery, synthesising user feedback into requirements, and a Computer Science degree is listed. Domain is construction finance (budgets, cost control), which he would need to learn. Posting only says applicants must work from the Dublin office; no sponsorship wording seen.

title: Product Designer (UI/UX)
note: Stretch: asks 3+ years. Fintech/insurance app; end-to-end flows, wireframes, prototypes, reusable components across web and mobile match his Mewurk work. Remote but candidates must already be based in Ireland (he is in Dublin); no sponsorship mentioned.

title: UX-UI Designer
note: Stretch: asks 3+ years, ideally agency. Digital agency for enterprise and public-sector clients; research, usability testing, wireframes, prototypes, hi-fi UI and design systems fit well. Right to work: 'Applicants must be eligible to work in Ireland' – check Stamp 1G timing.

title: Web Designer - UX, UI, CMS
note: Stretch: asks 3+ years in web and graphic design, plus hands-on CMS, email campaigns and some mentoring of junior web designers, none of which are on his CV. Fits his UX/UI principles, responsive design, Photoshop/Illustrator and marketing graphics work. Financial services client, fully remote but must be in Ireland. No right-to-work statement on the posting.
